subject: petroleum-engineering
intro: Petroleum engineering leads to the highest-paid engineering salaries in extraction and energy: drilling, reservoir and production specialists, and increasingly the subsurface experts of the energy transition.

roles.title: Petroleum Engineers
roles.what: Devise methods to improve oil and gas extraction and production, decide when new or modified tool designs are needed, oversee drilling operations and offer technical advice across the life of a well.
roles.where: This course is the role: drilling engineering covers rig systems and well control, reservoir engineering covers Darcy flow and recovery, production engineering covers artificial lift and completions, and formation evaluation covers the logging that steers it all.

roles.title: Geological Technicians, Except Hydrologic Technicians
roles.what: Assist scientists and engineers with electronic, sonic or nuclear measuring instruments in exploration and production, obtaining data on resources such as petroleum, and analysing mud, drill cuttings and well pressure and temperature charts.
roles.where: The formation evaluation unit — well logging, core analysis, volumetric reserves estimation — plus petroleum geology's porosity, permeability and reservoir-fluids work are exactly the measurements these technicians collect and chart.

roles.title: Mining and Geological Engineers, Including Mining Safety Engineers
roles.what: Conduct subsurface surveys to characterise potential land or mining development sites, specify ground support and equipment for safe, economical and environmentally sound extraction, and inspect for unsafe geological conditions.
roles.where: The geology unit's sedimentary basins, porosity and permeability, and the drilling unit's well control and cementing transfer directly to subsurface survey work, while the economics, safety and regulation topics ground the safety-engineering side.

roles.title: Chemical Engineers
roles.what: Apply chemistry, physics and engineering to solve problems involving the production of chemicals, fuels, drugs and food — designing processes and equipment that convert laboratory reactions into safe, large-scale manufacturing.
roles.where: The production engineering unit's flow assurance and stimulation chemistry, refining-adjacent reservoir-fluids work, and the economics and energy-transition unit's CCS topic are the doors from this syllabus into process and downstream roles.

roles.title: Engineering Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach university courses in the application of physical laws and engineering principles — including petroleum engineering specifically — combining classroom instruction with research on machines, materials, processes and services.
roles.where: Every unit here maps to lecture material, but reservoir simulation, well control and the energy-transition topics are the research fronts where faculty careers are built, supported by the volumetric estimation skills from formation evaluation.
